design_rationale: The paper describes a 12-week randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter phase IV trial in which symptomatic patients after a run-in were allocated to BUD/FM pMDI or BUD DPI via "computer-derived sequential allocation and stratification by asthma severity using balanced blocks."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind double-dummy design minimizes awareness-related deviations, but the analysis set was restricted to randomized patients who received ≥1 dose and contributed sufficient efficacy data (a modified ITT), and protocol-mandated withdrawal for asthma worsening differed in frequency between arms (18.9% vs 11.8%), so adherence/deviation handling is not fully transparent.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, 12-week phase IV study (NCT00702325)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated, stratified, block randomization in a double-blind double-dummy design with baseline characteristics generally balanced (minor imbalances in sex, BMI, and baseline ACT consistent with chance), although allocation concealment is not explicitly described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization was generated by computer-derived sequential allocation and stratification by asthma severity using balanced blocks."

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly all randomized patients contributed to the efficacy analyses (150/153 and 143/148), but differential withdrawal for asthma worsening (more in the BUD arm) combined with last-observation-carried-forward/treatment-period-mean analyses could bias between-group differences, and no sensitivity analysis for missingness is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Withdrawn due to a predefined event [n (%)]: 18 (11.8) ... 28 (18.9)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (predose FEV1) is an objective, standardized physiological measure assessed identically across arms under double-blind conditions, limiting assessor influence (though diary-based secondary outcomes are self-reported).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All spirometry measurements were conducted per ATS guidelines (15)." / "Predose spirometry testing was performed in the morning, ≥6 hours after the last rescue medication dose; testing occurred at the same time (±1 hour) at each assessment."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT00702325) with a clearly pre-specified primary endpoint and multiplicity control, but the full protocol/analysis plan is only in supplementary material, many secondary and subgroup analyses are reported selectively, and the study was sponsored and analyzed by AstraZeneca employees, leaving some concern about selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "To control for statistical testing multiplicity, a hierarchical step-down procedure was used."

overall_summary: Randomization and objective outcome measurement were well handled in this double-blind, double-dummy, registered trial, but differential protocol-mandated withdrawals for asthma worsening (18.9% vs 11.8%), a modified rather than full intention-to-treat analysis set, and sponsor-conducted analyses with numerous selectively reported secondary outcomes raise some concerns. The overall judgment is therefore "some concerns," driven by the deviations, missing-data, and selective-reporting domains.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "double-blind, randomised, active-controlled, parallel-group, stratified, multicentre study" with 438 patients randomised (146 per arm) to fluticasone/formoterol, SKP FP or GSK FP, registered as NCT00649025.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomisation with stratification by baseline FEV1 % predicted is reported and baseline demographic, lung-function and asthma-duration characteristics were closely balanced across the three equal-sized arms (146 each), consistent with chance; allocation-concealment mechanism is not described in detail but double-blind, identically primed pMDI treatment packs plus placebo inhalers imply concealed allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was a double-blind, randomised, active-controlled, parallel-group, stratified, multicentre study. Patients were stratified according to their percentage predicted forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV; either 40% to 60% or 460% to 80%)

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding with double-dummy placebo inhalers and an analysis "as randomised" on the full analysis population support low risk, but 36 patients had major protocol violations (26 met pre-specified discontinuation criteria yet were not discontinued) and at least one patient received the wrong treatment pack, and the asymmetric differential discontinuation for loss of asthma control (1 vs 9 vs 6) raises the possibility that the fast-onset bronchodilator effect of formoterol made the assignment partly discernible to patients/investigators.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty-six patients had major protocol violations. Of these, 26 patients had met the pre-specified discontinuation criteria, but were not actually discontinued. These patients were evenly distributed across the treatment groups and none of the major protocol violations were expected to affect the conclusions of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Overall completion was high (89.5%) and all 438 randomised patients were included in the full analysis population with LOCF imputation plus MMRM/per-protocol sensitivity analyses, but discontinuation was markedly differential (4.8% fluticasone/formoterol vs 15.1% SKP FP and 11.6% GSK FP) and was driven by loss of asthma control, so LOCF carrying forward pre-deterioration values could bias comparisons in favour of the combination.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Fewer patients prematurely discontinued from the study in the fluticasone/formoterol group (seven patients; 4.8%) compared to the SKP FP (22 patients; 15.1%) and GSK FP (17 patients; 11.6%) groups. The main reason for premature discontinuation was loss of asthma control

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is objective spirometry (FEV1) performed to ATS/ERS standards with the same standardised spirometer per patient at identical time points in all arms, under double-blind conditions, so outcome ascertainment is unlikely to have been influenced by knowledge of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pulmonary function test procedures were carried out in accordance with the American Thoracic Society (ATS)/European Respiratory Society (ERS) Guidelines using a standardised spirometer (Micromedical, Model MicroLab 3500). Each patient was to use the same spirometer throughout the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT00649025/EudraCT 2007-005653-37) with a clearly pre-specified primary endpoint, hierarchical gate-keeping scheme and pre-specified subgroup analysis, but the hierarchy broke at the first secondary endpoint and the paper nonetheless emphasises numerous exploratory/tertiary endpoints and a post hoc negative binomial annualised exacerbation rate analysis (reported as significant) to support the superiority claim; sponsor funding and authorship by sponsor employees add to the concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The annualised rate of asthma exacerbations was analysed post hoc using a negative binomial model. ... However, as the difference between fluticasone/formoterol and SKP FP was non-significant, all other endpoints were tested in an exploratory manner only.

overall_summary: This registered, double-blind, double-dummy randomised trial had sound allocation, balanced baseline characteristics and an objective, standardised spirometric primary outcome (D1 and D4 low risk). Overall risk is "some concerns" driven by differential discontinuation (4.8% vs 15.1%/11.6%) largely for loss of asthma control handled by LOCF, major protocol violations in 36 patients, and selective-reporting concerns arising from reliance on exploratory and post hoc analyses after the testing hierarchy failed at the first secondary endpoint in a sponsor-run, sponsor-authored study.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "52-week, international, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group study" in which eligible subjects meeting run-in symptom criteria "were randomized to receive FSC 250/50 mcg or FP 250 mcg twice daily" (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00452348).

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization after a run-in period is stated and baseline demographics, lung function, PEF, symptom-free days and ACT scores were closely matched between the two arms (consistent with chance), though the exact sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods are not described; the double-blind registered industry trial design makes concealment plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Those who met symptom-inclusion criteria for at least 2 of the last 7 days of the run-in period were randomized to receive FSC 250/50 mcg or FP 250 mcg twice daily." ... "Screening demographics and asthma characteristics were well matched between treatment groups (Table 1)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with both arms delivered via the same DISKUS device, median exposure and compliance were nearly identical (94.5% vs 93.8%), and all randomized subjects were analyzed under an intention-to-treat framework.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The intent-to-treat population, comprised of all randomized subjects, was used for all evaluations of eficacy and safety." ... "Mean % compliance (SD) 94.5 (13.76) | 93.8 (15.86)"

domain_judgments.rationale: 26% of subjects (163) withdrew prematurely over 52 weeks and, although reasons for withdrawal appear balanced between arms, the paper does not describe how missing longitudinal FEV1/diary data were handled (no imputation or sensitivity analysis reported), so bias from missingness cannot be fully excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "During the 52-week treatment period, 163 subjects (26%) were prematurely withdrawn from the study. Overall, the most common reasons for withdrawal in both groups were protocol violation (8%) and voluntary subject withdrawal (6%)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objective spirometric trough FEV1 measured identically across arms using ATS-compliant equipment and NHANES III reference values, with blinded participants and investigators, and diary outcomes captured by electronic diary/peak-flow meter.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Spirometry was conducted at 2-weeks post randomization and then on a monthly basis post-randomization using spirometry equipment at each site which met American Thoracic Society (ATS) recommendations."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT00452348) with a pre-specified primary endpoint, powered sample size and an a priori hierarchical/Hochberg multiplicity plan that the authors respected when declaring secondary endpoints non-significant; however, nominal p-values for secondary measures and post-hoc subgroup analyses by baseline percent-predicted are emphasized in the narrative, and the study was funded and co-authored by the manufacturer, raising some concern about selective emphasis in reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Since a significant treatment diference was not observed for the analysis of the primary eficacy measure, all comparisons for other eficacy measures were declared not statistically significant. However, results are provided to help inform on the outcome of the individual measures." ... "Study population post-hoc analysis conducted to compare pulmonary function at screening and baseline..."

overall_summary: This registered, double-blind, parallel-group RCT had well-matched arms, objective blinded spirometric outcomes and an ITT analysis with a pre-specified hierarchical testing plan (all low risk for D1, D2 and D4). Overall risk is "some concerns", driven by substantial 26% attrition over 52 weeks with no described handling of missing data (D3) and by reporting that emphasizes nominal secondary-endpoint p-values and post-hoc analyses in a sponsor-run, sponsor-authored trial (D5).

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "52-week, international, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group study" (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00452699) in which symptomatic subjects after run-in "were randomized to receive FSC 250/50 µg or FP 250 µg b.i.d."

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization and double-blinding are stated and most baseline variables are closely balanced, but no detail is given on sequence generation or allocation concealment, and there is a notable baseline imbalance in asthma duration ≥15 years (49% vs 61%) and mean age (36.8 vs 39.3 yr).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Those who were symptomatic during the last 7 days of the run-in period were randomized to receive FSC 250/50 -g or FP 250 -g b.i.d." ... "Screening demographics and asthma characteristics, including sex, race, age, asthma duration, and pulmonary function, were well matched between treatment groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: Both treatments were delivered double-blind via identical Diskus devices with high and comparable compliance, and the analysis was intention-to-treat on all randomized subjects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The analysis population was the ITT population, which included all subjects randomized to study drug." ... "mean treatment compliance, as derived from the Diskus dose counter, was 93% in both treatment groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: Roughly a quarter of participants withdrew in each arm (well above the 5% attrition anticipated in the power calculation), and although withdrawal reasons were reported as balanced, no imputation strategy or sensitivity analysis for missing data is described, and withdrawal per asthma criteria is itself outcome-related.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "During the 52-week treatment period 81 (26%) subjects treated with FSC 250/50 -g and 73 (23%) subjects from the FP 250 -g withdrew. The primary reasons for withdrawal were similar between treatment groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (trough predose FEV1) is an objective, standardized spirometric measure applied identically in both arms under double-blind conditions, minimizing assessor influence; diary-based secondary outcomes are self-reported but blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Spirometry was conducted on a monthly basis using the sites spirometry equipment, which met or exceeded American Thoracic Society recommendations."

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered and had a pre-specified hierarchical/Hochberg multiplicity plan with a clearly defined primary endpoint, the pre-specified secondary 'asthma attack' endpoint was null and the emphasized exacerbation, time-to-first-exacerbation and subgroup analyses were explicitly post hoc (acknowledged as only 'nominally' significant), raising concern about selective emphasis of reported results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A post hoc analysis was conducted to determine which of the asthma attack criterion contributed to the lack of significant difference between treatment arms for the asthma attack rate." ... "The time to first exacerbation was also examined in a post hoc analysis."

overall_summary: This large registered, double-blind, ITT-analysed trial with an objective primary outcome has low risk in the intervention-delivery and outcome-measurement domains, but raises some concerns from unreported allocation-sequence/concealment detail with minor baseline imbalances, ~25% attrition with no described handling of missing data, and heavy reliance on post hoc exacerbation analyses after the pre-specified 'asthma attack' endpoint was null. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a phase III, stratified, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in which subjects were "randomized in a 3:1 ratio between MDPI and the comparators for each cohort and dose strength" (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02175771).

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization with stratification by entry therapy and dose strength is stated and baseline demographics/spirometry appear similar, but the sequence generation method and allocation concealment are not described, and the authors themselves note that balance on an important prognostic factor (exacerbation history) could not be confirmed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The subjects were then randomized in a 3:1 ratio between MDPI and the comparators for each cohort and dose strength." ... "a history of asthma exacerbations was not collected, and, therefore, a balance in randomization could not be confirmed across the treatment groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label so subjects, investigators and care providers knew the assigned device, which could affect subjective symptom reporting, AE ascertainment and co-intervention/rescue medication use; analyses were based on all randomized subjects receiving at least one dose (approximately ITT) but adherence and deviations are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Due to the difficulty in blinding the active comparator treatments, an open-label study design had to be used for this safety and efficacy trial, which may limit the conclusiveness of the comparisons within and across the treatment groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: Spirometry is an objective outcome measured identically across groups, but the primary safety outcomes (AEs, investigator-defined exacerbation severity, causality) and subjective diary outcomes were assessed by unblinded investigators and participants, so outcome assessment could have been influenced by knowledge of the assigned device.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Mild and moderate asthma exacerbations were defined by the investigator." ... "Investigators characterized the relationship of AEs to the study drug."

domain_judgments.rationale: Numbers in the full analysis set are only slightly lower than randomized numbers and a disposition figure is provided, but withdrawal rates over the 26-week period and reasons by group are not reported in the text, and no sensitivity analysis for missing diary/spirometry data is described in this long open-label trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The full analysis set, including all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of study drug and had at least one postbaseline trough FEV assessment, was used for all efficacy analyses."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT02175771) with a pre-specified principal efficacy endpoint and noninferiority margin, but no protocol/SAP is cited for direct comparison, numerous outcomes are reported, and at least one post hoc analysis was performed to address an unfavorable exacerbation imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Post hoc analyses were conducted to determine if the incidence of asthma exacerbations was different across the treatment groups."

overall_summary: This registered, stratified, randomized phase III trial used objective spirometric endpoints and a pre-specified noninferiority margin, but it was entirely open-label, with investigator-rated adverse events and exacerbation severity, unreported allocation-concealment details, unconfirmed balance on exacerbation history, incompletely described attrition, and a post hoc exacerbation analysis. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is some concerns.

design_rationale: Explicitly a "12-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled US study (NCT 00419757)" in which "Randomization used a computer-generated allocation schedule" with 1:1 allocation within ICS dose strata.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated, stratified 1:1 allocation schedule was used in a double-blind design, and baseline demographic, pulmonary-function and ICS-dose characteristics were closely balanced between groups ("Demographic and key baseline characteristics were balanced among treatment groups"), consistent with adequate randomization, although concealment mechanics are not described in detail.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization used a computer-generated allocation schedule. The participants were stratified by asthma severity... Participants meeting entry criteria were randomized 1:1 within the appropriate ICS dose stratum

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind administration of both inhalers limits performance bias, but the analysis set was a modified ITT excluding randomized participants without efficacy data (125/127 and 119/123), adherence was not reported, and acknowledged study-conduct problems (inaccurate reporting of baseline ICS use, permitted rescreening) suggest implementation deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy analyses included participants who received 1 or more doses of study medication and contributed sufficient data for at least 1 efficacy end point.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants experiencing predefined asthma events were withdrawn and withdrawal rates differed by arm, yet the numeric completion figures (Figure 1) and methods for handling missing diary/PEF data are not described in the text, so bias from informative missingness cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Fewer participants receiving BUD/FM vs BUD had worsening asthma based on the predefined criteria (25.2% vs 31.7%) or were withdrawn (3.1% vs 6.5%)

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (AM PEF) is an objective, standardized measurement captured by identical devices and electronic diaries in both arms under double-blind conditions, so outcome assessment is unlikely to be differentially influenced despite being self-recorded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mini-Wright peak flow meters... and hand-held electronic diaries (LogPad, PHT Corporation, Massachusetts) were dispensed at screening. Participants used the electronic diary twice daily to record peak expiratory flow (PEF)

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT00419757) with a clearly prespecified primary endpoint and sample-size calculation, but multiple post hoc subgroup/outlier analyses—emphasized in the discussion after a null primary result—raise concerns about selective emphasis of favorable analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Exploratory post hoc analyses investigated the effect of outlier data on pulmonary function variables, assessed the effect of treatment in participants with stable or decreasing FEV during the run-in period, and stratified data for AM PEF and predose FEV by self-reported region of descent

overall_summary: This registered, double-blind, computer-randomized trial had a sound allocation process and an objective primary outcome, but incomplete reporting of participant flow/missing-data handling, a modified-ITT efficacy set with acknowledged study-conduct problems (unverified baseline ICS use, rescreening), and post hoc subgroup/outlier analyses emphasized after a null primary result raise some concerns. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: A 52-week, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter phase 3B trial (NCT00419952) in which 742 patients were randomized 1:1 using computer-generated sequential allocation with balanced blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated allocation with balanced blocks and concealment via identically packaged medication; baseline demographics and lung function were similar between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization occurred by using computer-generated sequential allocation; approximately equal distribution of patients per treatment group at each site was ensured by using balanced blocks. Allocation concealment was maintained by packaging the study medications identically, with the exception of the computer-generated randomization number."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind with identical devices, and the primary safety analysis included all randomized patients receiving ≥1 dose (approximating ITT), but protocol deviations were common (per-protocol set excluded ~17% of patients, mainly for not meeting ICS inclusion criteria) and adherence/co-intervention details (e.g., differential rescue and concomitant corticosteroid use) are incompletely reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Another possible limitation of the present study is the inclusion of patients who deviated from the study protocol in the primary safety analysis; however, similar results were observed after exclusion of patients who deviated from the protocol"

domain_judgments.rationale: Over a 52-week trial with an anticipated withdrawal rate of ~17% by month 6 and mean exposure of only 266 vs 287 days (suggesting differential discontinuation), dropout numbers and reasons are presented only in a figure, and no sensitivity analysis for missing continuous/diary outcomes is described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Mean treatment exposure was 266 and 287 days in the budesonide/formoterol and budesonide groups, respectively."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective or standardized (prespecified exacerbation criteria, spirometry per ATS standards, laboratory/ECG/Holter, electronic diaries) and measured identically in both groups under double-blind conditions, limiting assessor influence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Asthma exacerbations were defined as requirement of oral/parenteral corticosteroids and/or emergency department visit and/or urgent care visit and/or hospitalization for asthma."

domain_judgments.rationale: No single primary efficacy variable was defined and there were no prespecified hypotheses, with many outcome measures and unadjusted nominal P values reported, creating potential for selective emphasis among numerous eligible analyses (though the trial was registered and the protocol defined safety endpoints).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Designed as a safety study, no single efficacy variable was considered primary... Because there were no prespecified hypotheses in this study, all reported P values are nominal, without adjustment for multiple comparisons."

overall_summary: Randomization and outcome measurement were well executed (computer-generated allocation, concealed, double-blind, objective/standardized outcomes), but there are some concerns from frequent protocol deviations, long-term attrition with somewhat differential treatment exposure and limited handling of missing data, and absence of a prespecified primary endpoint with many unadjusted comparisons. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns," driven by the worst domain judgments (D2, D3, D5).

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation 1:1:1 to FF-VI, FF, or placebo using a central, computer-generated randomization schedule (RandAll) in a phase III double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central computer-generated allocation schedule with a registration/medication ordering system ensured concealment, and baseline demographics and lung function were well balanced across the three arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The central randomization schedule was generated by the sponsor by using a validated computerized system (RandAll; Glaxo-SmithKline, London, UK), and the patients were randomized by using Registration and Medication Ordering System."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind administration via identical dry powder inhalers with patients, investigators and technical staff blinded, and analysis was conducted in the intent-to-treat population.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients, investigators, and technical staff were blinded to treatment assignment." ... "Data for the intent-to-treat (ITT) population (defined as all patients who were randomized to treatment and who received at least 1 dose of study drug) are reported"

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 85% completed, with markedly differential withdrawal for lack of efficacy (16% placebo vs 3% active) handled by LOCF imputation, and the co-primary 0-24 h wmFEV1 was available for only 51% of randomized patients (vs ~60% planned) and AQLQ for 73% of the placebo arm; the authors themselves note dropout may have inflated the placebo response.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The differential rate of dropout between the placebo and the active treatment groups may also have contributed to the observed high placebo response."

domain_judgments.rationale: Co-primary outcomes were objective spirometric measures (trough and serial FEV1) obtained identically across arms with patients, investigators and technical staff blinded, minimizing assessor influence; data-quality problems at 2 of 64 sites were addressed by a sensitivity analysis that did not alter conclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients, investigators, and technical staff were blinded to treatment assignment."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT01165138) with prespecified co-primary endpoints and a prespecified closed step-down hierarchy controlling multiplicity; post hoc analyses are explicitly labelled and the decision to retain ITT as the primary population was documented before the sensitivity analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The decision that the ITT population would remain the primary population for presentation of results was documented before conducting the sensitivity analyses."

overall_summary: Well-conducted, registered, double-blind, centrally randomized phase III trial with objective spirometric outcomes and prespecified hierarchical testing; the only notable issue is missing outcome data — 15% non-completion with strongly differential withdrawal for lack of efficacy in the placebo arm (16% vs 3%), LOCF imputation, and only ~51% of patients contributing to the serial wmFEV1 co-primary endpoint, which the authors acknowledge may have influenced the efficacy assessment. This yields an overall judgment of some concerns.

design_rationale: The paper describes a "double-blind, double-dummy, 24-week randomised clinical trial" in which 645 patients were "randomised to receive one of three treatments," with randomisation "performed according to a balanced block design with a centrally generated randomisation code" (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00476268).

domain_judgments.rationale: Centrally generated balanced block randomisation code implies concealed allocation, and baseline characteristics (age, sex, FEV1, PEF, symptom-free days, prior ICS dose) were closely similar across the three groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomisation was performed according to a balanced block design with a centrally generated randomisation code. Blocks of three randomisation numbers were allocated to each centre." ... "Baseline characteristics were similar between groups, as shown in Table 1."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind, double-dummy design with three inhalers (active or placebo) per patient maintained blinding of participants and investigators, and efficacy was analysed in the ITT population (supported by PP analyses).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Each participant received three inhalers (containing active drug or placebo) to maintain blinding while using inhalers of different appearance." ... "Efficacy data were analysed for both the intention to treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) populations."

domain_judgments.rationale: 92.4% of randomised patients completed 24 weeks with balanced withdrawals, and missing data were handled by last-observation-carried-forward within an ITT analysis, making bias from attrition unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 824 patients were screened and 645 were randomised to treatment, of whom 596 (92.4%) completed the 24-week study." ... "The last available post-baseline values were carried forward to the end of treatment time point for missing data."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (morning PEF) was objectively recorded with an electronic peak flow meter identically in all groups under double-blind conditions, so outcome assessment was unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of allocation; the more subjective symptom/control diary outcomes were also collected blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients recorded their PEF with an electronic peak flow meter (Spirotel, MIR, Italy)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered and the primary endpoint pre-specified, several headline claims (superior asthma control, exacerbation reduction) rest on explicitly post-hoc analyses with multiple outcome operationalisations and no adjustment for multiplicity, and the sponsor was involved in analysis and manuscript drafting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Additionally, a post-hoc analysis was performed by assessing asthma control as: no nocturnal awakenings, no asthma symptoms and no rescue medication used." ... "For the secondary efficacy variables the adjustment was not considered necessary being these used for supportive purpose only."

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted for its pre-specified primary endpoint (central block randomisation, double-blind double-dummy, 92% completion, objective PEF measurement, ITT analysis), so domains 1–4 are at low risk. Overall judgment is "some concerns" because key secondary conclusions on asthma control and exacerbations derive from post-hoc, unadjusted multiple analyses in a sponsor-analysed study, raising the possibility of selective reporting of results.

design_rationale: Explicitly a "12-week, randomised, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, stratified, parallel-group study" with allocation by minimisation with biased coin assignment via an Interactive Voice Response System (NCT00393952).

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind design with matching dummy placebo inhalers kept patients, site staff, monitors and sponsor blinded, compliance was high (86.8%), and analyses were conducted on a full analysis set including essentially all randomised, dosed patients (543/557).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "blinding was maintained throughout the study with the use of dummy placebo inhalers. All investigators, personnel at the study site, and representatives involved in monitoring, data management and any other aspect of the trial, including sponsor personnel, were blinded throughout the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used minimisation with biased-coin assignment administered centrally through an Interactive Voice Response System (concealing allocation), with stratification on prognostic factors, and the five groups were well balanced on demographics and baseline lung function.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomised according to minimisation with biased coin assignment and treatment groups were balanced on baseline FEV % predicted (40%e60% or >60%e80%), study site, and the subgroup of patients aged 12e18 years. An Interactive Voice Response System was used for subject enrolment and treatment allocation"

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly 30% of patients discontinued prematurely with markedly differential attrition across arms (e.g., 39% lack of efficacy in placebo vs 10% in combination) and missing spirometry/diary data were handled only by last-observation-carried-forward without sensitivity analyses, so some bias in the continuous endpoints cannot be excluded (though LOCF is likely conservative against the combination).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In total, 395 (70.9%) patients completed the study and 162 (29.1%) discontinued... Missing observed data for both the primary and secondary efficacy analyses were managed using last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes were objective, standardised spirometric measurements (ATS/ERS standardisation, predicted values by established equations) assessed identically across blinded arms; patient-reported diary outcomes were also collected under blinding via a telephone diary system.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "FEV was measured at baseline and at weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12, and the predicted FEV values from Polgar and Promadhat and Crapo et al were used"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT00393952/EudraCT 2006-005989-39) with clearly pre-specified co-primary endpoints, a pre-defined sequential gatekeeper testing hierarchy for secondary endpoints, and transparent labelling of uncontrolled tertiary p-values, although the full protocol was not available for verification.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "If all three co-primary endpoints were statistically significant then the secondary endpoints were evaluated in a confirmatory manner using a sequential gatekeeper approach."

overall_summary: A well-conducted, registered, double-blind, centrally randomised phase 3 trial with objective spirometric primary outcomes and pre-specified hierarchical testing, so most domains are at low risk. The overall rating of "some concerns" is driven by the high (29%) and differential discontinuation rate handled solely with LOCF imputation and no sensitivity analyses; industry sponsorship/authorship is an additional, non-domain consideration.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation is described: "patients were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) via interactive response technology" in a 52-week multicentre, double-blind, triple-dummy, parallel-group phase 3 trial, with stratification by age and geographical region.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central interactive response technology randomization with stratification ensures a concealed allocation sequence, and baseline characteristics (age, sex, ACQ-7, FEV1 % predicted, reversibility, exacerbation history) were closely balanced across all five arms, consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "At the end of run-in visit, patients were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) via interactive response technology... Randomisation was stratified by age (12–17 years or ≥18 years) and geographical region... Patients, investigator staf, personnel doing the assessments, and data analysts remained masked to the identity of the treatment from the time of randomisation until the database lock."

domain_judgments.rationale: A rigorous triple-dummy double-blind design masked participants, site staff, assessors and analysts, and the primary analysis followed the randomized assignment (modified intention-to-treat full analysis set), with similar treatment exposure across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In order to maintain the blinded nature of the study, all the participants were required to use all the three inhalers in a day... The identity of the treatment was additionally concealed by the use of study drugs that were all identical in packaging, labelling schedule of administration, appearance, taste, and odour (triple-dummy)... For analysis based on the full analysis set, patients were analysed according to the treatment they were assigned to at randomisation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 11% discontinued treatment over 52 weeks and the MMRM relies on an unverified missing-at-random assumption, with the most common discontinuation reason being asthma exacerbation (an outcome-related cause that was more frequent in the MF monotherapy arms) and no reported sensitivity analysis for missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "2216 patients were randomly assigned... of which 1973 (89·0%) completed the study treatment and 234 (10·6%) prematurely discontinued study treatment... The MMRM model assumes the missing at random mechanism for missing values."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (trough FEV1) is an objective, centrally standardised spirometric measure applied identically across arms under maintained blinding, with independent adjudication of serious asthma outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Spirometry was standardised by means of centralised spirometry and the results were analysed in accordance with American Thoracic Society–European Respiratory Society (ATS–ERS) criteria for acceptability and repeatability... an independent external adjudication committee was established to assess these outcomes."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with the protocol and statistical analysis plan made available, the primary and key secondary endpoints were prespecified with a predefined non-inferiority margin (−90 mL) and formal family-wise error control, and results are reported in line with the registered plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02554786... The protocol is included in appendix 2... To control the family-wise type-I error rate at the two-sided 5% significance level, a multiple testing procedure based on the trimmed Simes test used by Brannath and colleagues (2009) was used."

overall_summary: This large, centrally randomized, triple-dummy double-blind phase 3 trial had low risk of bias for randomization, deviations from intended interventions, outcome measurement (objective centralised spirometry), and selection of the reported result (prospective registration, published protocol, prespecified endpoints and multiplicity control). The overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven solely by missing outcome data, with ~10.6% premature treatment discontinuation handled by MMRM under an untested missing-at-random assumption and discontinuations partly due to asthma exacerbations that were unevenly distributed across arms.

design_rationale: Explicit 1:1 random allocation via a computer-generated schedule and automated telephone randomisation system in a phase III double-blind parallel-group trial (NCT01086384).

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated allocation sequence with central telephone randomisation ensures concealment, and baseline demographics, lung function and exacerbation history were closely balanced between the two arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomised using an automated interactive telephone-based system (RAMOS; GlaxoSmithKline, UK) in accordance with a computer-generated schedule (RandAll; GlaxoSmithKline, UK)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind delivery via identical dry powder inhalers with restriction of non-study ICS, and primary analysis was ITT, with a PP analysis giving concordant results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This phase III randomised, multicentre, double-blind, parallel-group study... All efficacy and safety analyses were carried out in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population"

domain_judgments.rationale: Time-to-event analysis included all randomised patients and informative censoring was formally explored with similar results, but withdrawal numbers (assumed ~10% loss to follow-up, with an event-driven variable-duration design) are only shown in a figure/appendix and some FEV1 endpoint data will be missing for early withdrawals.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The possibility of informative censoring was explored. The Kaplan–Meier curves for time to first severe asthma exacerbation or withdrawal due to lack of efficacy, investigator discretion or withdrawal of consent between the two treatment groups did not differ from those of the primary analysis"

domain_judgments.rationale: Severe exacerbations were defined by standard ERS/ATS criteria and confirmed by a blinded independent adjudication committee, with FEV1 measured objectively and identically in both blinded arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A blinded independent adjudication committee ensured that all severe asthma exacerbations were captured as defined in the protocol."

domain_judgments.rationale: Pre-registered protocol with pre-specified primary/secondary endpoints and interim analysis adjustment, but the trial was sponsored, analysed and co-authored by GlaxoSmithKline employees and many "other endpoints" are relegated to an online appendix, so complete fidelity to the pre-specified analysis plan cannot be fully verified from the report.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary endpoint was time to first severe exacerbation; secondary endpoints were rate of severe asthma exacerbations per patient per year and change in trough evening forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV) from baseline."

overall_summary: This large, registered, double-blind, centrally randomised phase III trial had strong allocation concealment, blinded independent outcome adjudication and ITT analysis, but residual concerns arise from incompletely reported withdrawal/missing-data detail under the variable-duration event-driven design and from sponsor involvement in analysis and reporting with several endpoints presented only in an online appendix. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns" rather than low.
